4.2.2 Qualifications are judged on their content and level, not on the name or prestige of the institution.

4.4.3 If equivalence of an overseas qualification cannot be judged from the application, the assessor records "information missing: qualification equivalence" and refers to the Recruiter. The applicant is not scored as having no qualification.

4.4.4 An applicant's name, country of birth, accent or language background must not influence any score. Part-time, casual and contract roles count for their full calendar duration and are not pro-rated. Overlapping roles are not double-counted.

4.1.2 For the Payroll Officer role (E1), only experience in which the applicant was responsible for processing payroll counts towards the minimum period. Processing payroll means calculating wages and running pay cycles, not only checking or entering data.

4.1.3 Experience described as "assisting", "supporting the payroll team", "checking timesheets" or "entering payroll data" is relevant but is partial evidence. It scores at most 1 for E1, however long it lasted.

4.1.4 Where the duration of the relevant experience cannot be worked out, for example because dates are missing, score what the evidence supports and record "information missing: dates of payroll experience".

4.1.5 Years of experience are not a stand-in for maturity or age. 1.2 This policy applies to every stage of recruitment, including screening done with software or artificial intelligence (AI).

2.3 The People & Culture Manager owns this policy and must approve any change to screening criteria, prompts or scoring rules used by screening tools."}]}]

tool_calls.query: career break employment gap scoring policy
tool_calls.observation:
[{"query":"career break employment gap scoring policy","method":"BM25 keyword search","results":[{"chunk_id":"POL-GAPS","source":"Melbourne Business Services - Recruitment and Selection Policy (fictional)","section":"4.3 Career breaks and gaps in employment","title":"Career breaks must not be scored negatively","score":16.4,"text":"4.3.1 A career break or gap in employment, of any length and for any reason or none, must not lower any score and must not be mentioned as a weakness.

4.3.2 Applicants do not have to explain a gap. Assessors must not guess at the reason, such as parenting, illness or age, because such guesses relate to protected attributes (parental or carer status, disability, age).

4.3.3 Experience gained before a career break counts in full towards the experience criteria. None of the MBS Payroll Officer criteria require recent experience. Assessors must therefore not add a recency requirement that is not in the advertisement.

4.3.4 If the assessor believes that knowledge may have changed during a break, for example award rates or payroll legislation, this is recorded as a question for interview. It is never a deduction at screening.

4.3.5 Basis: indirect discrimination provisions of the Sex Discrimination Act 1984 (Cth) and the Equal Opportunity Act 2010 (Vic). Career breaks are taken disproportionately by women and carers."},{"chunk_id":"POL-PURPOSE","source":"Melbourne Business Services - Recruitment and Selection Policy (fictional)","section":"1 Purpose and scope; 2 Roles","title":"Purpose of the policy and who makes hiring decisions","score":7.15,"text":"1.1 Melbourne Business Services (MBS) selects staff on merit, by assessing each applicant's evidence against the selection criteria published in the job advertisement. Nothing else is assessed.

1.2 This policy applies to every stage of recruitment, including screening done with software or artificial intelligence (AI).

2.1 The Recruiter for the vacancy is accountable for the shortlist. The Hiring Manager makes the final appointment decision.

2.2 Screening tools, including the AI pre-screening workflow, provide decision support only. A tool may recommend, but it may not reject an applicant, appoint an applicant or contact an applicant. Every decision not to progress an applicant must be confirmed by the Recruiter, who records the reason.

2.3 The People & Culture Manager owns this policy and must approve any change to screening criteria, prompts or scoring rules used by screening tools."},{"chunk_id":"POL-AI-SCREENING","source":"Melbourne Business Services - Recruitment and Selection Policy (fictional)","section":"7 Use of AI-assisted screening","title":"Rules for AI-assisted screening - human review, routing, testing and records","score":4.99,"text":"7.1 The AI pre-screening workflow routes each application to one of three outcomes:
- shortlist, where every essential criterion scores 2 or more and nothing is flagged;
- Recruiter to confirm rejection;
- Recruiter review, which covers everything else, including borderline, flagged and low-confidence cases.

7.2 Every AI score must quote the applicant's words, and every legal or policy statement must cite the policy or legal source relied on.

7.3 Applicants are told in the job advertisement that AI-assisted screening is used, and that they may ask for their application to be reviewed by a person.

7.4 Before first use, and every six months after that, the People & Culture Manager arranges a bias test. Equivalent applications that differ only in name, gender, age indicators or career breaks must receive the same outcomes. Any systematic difference stops use of the tool until it is fixed.

7.5 Each run is logged with the date, models used, scores and reasons. Logs are kept for 12 months and then deleted, in line with section 8."},{"chunk_id":"POL-SCORING","source":"Melbourne Business Services - Recruitment and Selection Policy (fictional)","section":"3.1-3.4 Scoring against selection criteria","title":"Scoring scale, evidence rule and shortlisting threshold","score":3.82,"text":"3.1 Each selection criterion is scored separately, using only evidence in the application:
- 0 = no evidence;
- 1 = partial evidence (related but incomplete, or the required level is not shown);
- 2 = meets the criterion;
- 3 = clearly exceeds the criterion.

3.2 Every score above 0 must be supported by the applicant's own words. Assessors must not assume skills that are not stated. They must also not mark down a skill because it is described briefly, if the description clearly shows the skill.

3.3 An applicant is shortlisted only if every essential criterion scores 2 or more. Desirable criteria are used only to rank applicants who meet all essential criteria. A low desirable score never removes an applicant.

3.4 Where a criterion cannot be scored confidently from the application, the assessor scores what the evidence supports, records "information missing" with the specific question to ask, and refers the application to the Recruiter. Uncertainty is never resolved against the applicant."}]}]

tool_calls.query: Modern Awards National Employment Standards scoring policy

reviewer.critique: Score D1 must be corrected from 2 to 3. Per POL-EQUIV section 4.2.3, experience with a single recognised payroll system (MYOB) meets D1 and scores 2. However, the applicant demonstrates experience with BOTH MYOB AND Microsoft Excel for payroll verification, and the policy explicitly states 'Experience with more than one system, or with administering or implementing a system, may score 3.' Since MYOB and Excel are two different systems both used for payroll work, this should score 3, not 2. The current rationale incorrectly states the score as 2 when the evidence supports 3.
concerns: D1 score of 2 is inconsistent with policy POL-EQUIV 4.2.3 which allows score 3 for experience with more than one system

The applicant's experience spans Jan 2019–Dec 2022 (4 years), but the role end date is Dec 2022 with a career break from Jan 2023–Dec 2025, making the application current as of late 2025 or 2026; policy POL-GAPS 4.3.3 confirms experience before a break counts in full and no recency requirement exists
E1 score of 3 is appropriate: 4 years of payroll processing clearly exceeds the 2-year requirement per POL-EXPERIENCE 4.1.2
All other scores (E2, E3, E4, D2) are correctly supported by resume evidence and policy citations

reviewer.critique: D2 score must be corrected from 2 to 3. The evidence quote directly states the applicant 'Applied relevant Modern Awards and National Employment Standards (NES) when calculating employee entitlements', which demonstrates clear knowledge and practical application of both Modern Awards and NES. This exceeds the desirable criterion requirement and merits a score of 3, not 2. The rationale correctly identifies that the criterion is met, but the score assigned contradicts this conclusion. Additionally, the kb_ref 'POL-OVERSEAS' is incorrect for D2; this criterion is about knowledge of Australian employment law, not overseas qualifications, and POL-OVERSEAS is about assessing overseas credentials—not relevant here.
concerns: D2 score is 2 but rationale states criterion is 'met', which typically corresponds to score 2, yet the evidence shows applied knowledge (calculation of entitlements), suggesting score 3 is more appropriate
D2 kb_ref cites POL-OVERSEAS, which addresses overseas qualifications and experience equivalence, not knowledge of Modern Awards and NES
E3 kb_ref cites POL-EQUIV for Excel skills assessment, but POL-EQUIV section 4.2.4 applies specifically to E3 and supports the score; however the reference is correctly applied
No issue with career break handling—correctly not penalized per POL-GAPS
